question: At the 16th European Nuclear Energy Forum on 6-7 November, European Commissioner for Energy, Kadri Simson, expressed her support for setting up a European alliance on SMRs1, which would allow the EU to continue showing ‘technological leadership’ and safeguard its ‘strategic autonomy’ in the field of energy2.
On 21 November, the European Parliament adopted the NZIA3, which includes SMRs in the European support programme for ‘green industries’4.

This is particularly important in view of the advances made in this area by Russia5 and China6, as well as the United States, which is already setting foot on the European market with SMRs from the US groups NuScale Power and Westinghouse due to be launched in Romania, Slovakia, Poland7, Sweden, Finland and Bulgaria8.

Significant state aid has allowed for the technological and commercial development of SMRs in the United States, including recent allocations granted under the Inflation Reduction Act. Does the Commission think it would be appropriate to allow similar projects in the European nuclear industry to benefit from European funding for research, in particular under the Horizon Europe programme?

answer: The Commission acknowledges the important role that small modular reactors (SMRs), can play in the decarbonisation of energy systems in those Member States that envisage SMRs as part of the solutions for their future energy needs (9). The Commission is taking the necessary steps to promptly launch the EU Industrial Alliance on SMRs, in order to strengthen the EU’s industrial and technological leadership globally.
The Commission’s priority is to ensure that nuclear power, including SMRs is deployed in line with the highest standards of nuclear safety, security and safeguards.

The latest Euratom Research and Training Programme (10) has supported research for enhancing safety features of the SMR technologies by allocating EUR 40 million to various research projects already approved and additional EUR 27 million is planned for the period 2023-2025 (11).

Nuclear activities are also included in the scope of several legal instruments adopted or under discussion, such as the Taxonomy Complementary Delegated Act (12), the reform of the Electricity Market Design (13) or the Net-Zero Industry Act (14) proposal. These instruments support investments in EU’s manufacturing industry, including the nuclear one.

The Commission assesses, as necessary, Member States’ measures, including those related to nuclear projects, under EU State aid rules. For example, on 7 December 2022, the Commission approved a EUR 50 million French aid measure to support a SMR research and development project (Nuward) of the Électricité de France.
